thread:
lee: follow-up from tonight's midnight flurry — dropping action items so we can track ownership. saw a recurring pattern: short CPU spikes on a subset of hosts causing duplicate pages from metric and anomaly rules.

sam: I can take ownership of the pager-rule dedupe change. plan: bump dedupe to 20m, add dedupe-key by host + service, and monitor for 7 days. ETA 48h.

annie: I'll own the alert threshold change for the NodeHighCpu rule. propose `avg_over_time(...[2m]) > 0.9` with `for: 4m`. small PR with test harness. ETA 72h.

lee: can we add a lightweight anomaly filter that ignores spikes <3m? tj uses a neat classifier but we don't need full ML here. even a simple duration check would cut noise.

annie: agreed. I'll add a step to the PR: run synthetic 90s spike test and confirm no page. add that to the acceptance tests.

pager-bot: reminder: changes to paging/dedupe require a monitored rollout window and a one-hour post-change observation.

sre-manager: suggest creating two tickets: quick wins (dedesign + for) and infra work (exporter smoothing + spike aggregation). mark quick wins P0.

sam: created board cards and assigned owners. added notes: rollback plan, acceptance tests, metric to monitor (`pages/hour` and `mean-time-to-alert`).

lee: also note pattern appears mostly between 00:30-03:30 UTC on hosts in zone-eu-2. may be a cron/backup overlap. can infra team check cron schedules? owner: infra-ops, ETA 1 week.

annie: posting PR link when ready. will include exact alert snippet and test commands.

sre-manager: good. after changes run a 14-day noise delta and report. target: >50% reduction in duplicate pages without increasing time-to-detect for real incidents.

lee: thanks all. let's reconvene in 10 days for results and decide next steps.
